data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Preferring the better-corroborated theory is defensible on Popper's own terms not as an inductive inference of future success, but as a critical methodological decision to act on the theory that has withstood the most severe attempts at falsification, thereby maximizing our current proximity to truth (verisimilitude) while explicitly acknowledging the risk of error.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the agent treats the survival of past tests as a probabilistic guarantee of future performance, the preference becomes inductive and violates Popper's core tenet.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the concept of verisimilitude is invoked as a measurable quantity rather than a regulative ideal, the Tich\u00fd-Miller refutation renders the justification invalid.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the preference is framed as a logical deduction that the better-corroborated theory is 'more likely true,' it smuggles in the very induction Popper rejected.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism is 'Critical Preferential Selection': agents treat corroboration reports not as probability scores but as comparative records of survival. When action is required, the agent voluntarily adopts the theory with the highest degree of corroboration because it is the one that has been most rigorously tested and not yet eliminated. This preference is a non-cognitive, volitional commitment to the aim of science (truth), distinguishing the logical status of the theory (still conjectural) from the pragmatic necessity of choosing the best available option without invoking induction.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
